Ikeja Electric has warned members of the public against illegal electricity connections, meter bypasses and tampering with electrical installations, describing the practices as threats to lives, infrastructure and electricity supply. The electricity distribution company urged residents to report suspicious activities and illegal connections to help protect the power network and prevent avoidable damage. Ikeja Electric gave the warning in a public advisory released on Wednesday on its X handle, stressing that electricity-related offences could endanger customers and affect the reliability of electricity supply. “Illegal electricity connections, meter bypasses and tampering with electrical installations come at a cost to everyone. They threaten lives, damage critical infrastructure and put other customers at risk,” the company stated. The company called on residents to remain vigilant and report any suspected cases of electricity theft or interference with its installations. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Members of the public can contact Ikeja Electric through 02-017000250 or 02-012272940. Reports can also be sent through its customer care email address, [email protected] . The company reiterated the importance of collective responsibility in protecting electricity infrastructure and promoting safety across its network. “Together, we can promote a safer and more reliable electricity network,” it added. Ikeja Electric urged residents to make use of the available reporting channels whenever they observe suspicious activities involving electricity installations.
